messages: USER

Build "IndexBoard": a free template that turns any evaluation results into an Artificial-Analysis-style leaderboard page.

Users: AI researchers, students and teams who compare models, tools or methods and want a professional, honest results page in minutes.

Core features:
1. Create a board: title, description, and a list of items (models) with scores per metric. Paste JSON or CSV, or fill a simple table. Provide a "Load example" button with realistic sample data (6 models, 4 metrics: Accuracy, Coverage, Cost per run in CNY, Median time in minutes; each score may have a 95% interval low/high and a run count).
2. The board page: a hero with title and four stat tiles; tabs Index, Models, Methodology.
   - Index tab: horizontal bar charts with a 95% interval whisker, one chart per metric, a scatter plot of score vs cost with a dashed "nobody beats" frontier line, and a banner "Statistical tie at the top" when the top intervals overlap.
   - Models tab: sortable table with every metric, a tie marker, and sticky header.
   - Methodology tab: shows the formula text the author typed (markdown), a worked example, and a "what is held fixed" list.
3. Honest by default: if intervals overlap the page says the order is not meaningful.
4. Save boards in the Atoms Cloud database with a public share link per board (read only) and an edit key for the owner. Without login, boards are anonymous.
5. English and Chinese: a language toggle (EN / 中文) that translates all interface text.
6. Light and dark mode following the system, mobile friendly (no horizontal page scroll at 390px width).
7. Export: copy the board as a PNG-friendly print view and download the data as JSON.

Design: clean, professional, calm blue and neutral palette, serif headline (Fraunces) with IBM Plex Sans body, generous spacing, no emoji. Charts drawn with inline SVG. No external chart library needed.

IndexBoard is built and you can try it in the App Viewer. The code checks and build pass, and a visual check of the home page passed. I haven't tested the full create, share and edit flow end to end, and dark mode and the 390px phone layout haven't been checked visually yet. Those are worth a quick look.

- **Creating a board:** you add a title, description and methodology, then enter results in a table, paste JSON, or paste CSV. CSV columns like "Accuracy low", "Accuracy high" and "Accuracy runs" are read as the interval and run count. "Load example" fills in 6 models and the 4 metrics you described (Accuracy, Coverage, Cost per run in CNY, Median time in minutes), each with intervals and run counts. Bad input gets a clear error before saving, and you can preview the board first.
- **Board page:** the hero has the title and four stat tiles, followed by three tabs:
  - **Index:** one bar chart per metric with 95% interval whiskers, the score-vs-cost scatter with a dashed "Nobody beats" frontier line, and a "Statistical tie at the top" banner when the top intervals overlap.
  - **Models:** a sortable table with every metric, "tied" markers and a sticky header.
  - **Methodology:** your formula text (markdown), the worked example, and the "what is held fixed" list.
- **Honest by default:** a model counts as tied when its 95% interval overlaps the leader's, and the banner, tiles, chart notes and table all say so. If no intervals are given, the page says the order is provisional.
- **Sharing and editing:** boards are saved to the Atoms Cloud database. Publishing gives you a read-only public link and a private edit key. The key can't be recovered if lost; your browser remembers it, and anyone else must paste it to edit. No login is needed, and the edit key stays hidden from the public link.
- **Language and display:** the EN / 中文 toggle translates all interface text, including the example data. Light and dark mode follow the system setting.
- **Export:**
  - **Print view:** a flat, light layout made for screenshots and saving as PDF.
  - **"Copy PNG" on each chart:** copies the chart as a picture. If the browser blocks copying, it downloads the PNG instead.
  - **JSON download:** saves the board's data, and the same file can be pasted back in to re-import it.

When you're happy with it, click Publish to deploy and share the link. If anything looks off or behaves unexpectedly, tell me what you see.
